To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1,25D3 stimulates the transfer of phosphatidyl choline from liposomes to renal brush border membrane vesicles, and this effect is mediated by 1,2D3 receptors.

1,25-(OH)2D3 and 24,25-(OH)(2)D3 stimulate the transfer of NBD-phosphatidylcholines from liposomes to brush border membrane vesicles, and that the effect is dose dependent, with maximum stimulation at 10-14 M.

1,25-(OH)2D3, 24,25(OH)(2)D3, 25(OH)3D3, and 1,25,27(OH)3, but not vitamin D3, stimulate phosphatidycholine transfer to rat renal brush-border membranes, and that the effect of 1,24(OH)2 is maximal at 10(-7)M and 2.5 X 10(-14).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism by which 1,25-(OH)2D3 affects the renal brush-border membrane.
the mechanism of the vitamin D effect on renal and intestinal ion transport and the effect of vitamin D on the phospholipid content of these brush-border membranes.
the effect of 1, 25-dihydroxycalciferol (1.25 (OH) 2D3) on phospholipid transfer to renal brush border membrane vesicles (BBMV) from liposomes containing self-quenched fluorescent phospholipids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
1,25 (OH)2D3, 24,25 (OH), and 25 (OH)3 stimulate the transfer of phospholipids from donor liposomes to renal brush-border membrane.

1,25-(OH)2D3, 25(OH)3 and 24,25-(OH)-D3 stimulate transfer of phosphatidyl-choline from liposomes to renal brush-border membrane, which in turn increases the phosphatidyl choline content of the membrane.
1,25D(3) stimulates phosphatidyl-choline transfer between liposomes and renal brush-border membrane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
1,25D3 stimulates the transfer of phospholipids to the renal brush border membrane.
1,25-(OH)2D3 stimulates phospholipid transfer to renal brush border membranes, and that this may be a mechanism for the hormone's effect on renal ion transport and phospholipid content.

1,25 (OH)2D3, 25(OH) D3, and 24,25 (OH)(2)D3 stimulate phosphatidycholine transfer from liposomes to renal brush-border membrane and that the transfer process may be involved in the regulation of renal ion transport.
The main takeaway from our work is that
1,25-D3 stimulates the transfer of phosphatidyl choline from liposomes to renal brush border membrane vesicles.
1,25D3 stimulates phosphatidyl-choline transfer from liposome to renal BBM.
1,25-(OH)2-D3 stimulates the transfer of phosphatidyl choline to renal brush-border membrane.
